title: Evaluation as Evolution: Transforming Adversarial Diffusion into Closed-Loop Curricula for Autonomous Vehicles

control_signal.value: Adversarial objective of reaching ego failure, with a scheduled adversarial intensity eta_r that sets how far samples may deviate from the nominal prior; a sparse set of critical agents is selected automatically.

control_mechanism.value: Transport-regularised drift controller optimised at inference time over a frozen reverse-time SDE prior, restricted to topology-selected agents; a feasibility-filtered coarse proposal is injected at an intermediate denoising step (Topological Anchoring).

base_model.value: Frozen pretrained diffusion trajectory model giving the nominal reverse-time SDE prior; closed-loop multi-agent simulator (BITS-style) with black-box ego policies (lane-graph, IDM, BITS).

datasets.value: nuScenes and nuPlan validation splits, vehicle-to-vehicle interactions; deployed on nuPlan without retraining.

metrics.value: Safety: Collision Failure Rate, MinDTC, Relative Impact Velocity, Rear-Impact Rate, TTC cost, mean acceleration. Realism/validity: All-Off-Road rate, REAL (Wasserstein-based fidelity score). Mean over 7 seeds.

controllability_evidence.value: Against baselines on nuScenes: CFR 60.29%, AOR 0.14%, REAL 0.7432; nuPlan CFR 78.57% vs 57.14% for Safe-Sim-opt. Ablation: Topo+Feas. 53.57% CFR vs Random-K 28.57%.

notes: Controls adversarial failure discovery and intensity rather than user-specified semantic attributes. Packet has no limitations section; only a safety-comfort trade-off in downstream policy fine-tuning (page 11). Includes policy-fine-tuning curriculum.
